thread:
Incident Bot: paging: Severity P1 - multiple Private VPC customers in eu-west1 experiencing cross-region routing + 5xx errors. Auto-assign -> Alex Grady (on-call)
Alex Grady: I'm on it. Seeing alerts: spike in 502/503 from rear-end for requests that normally hit eu-west1 ILB. Latency up ~3-5s for some tenants. Root cause unknown. @Maya can you check GCP LB health and control plane? Paging @Sam for tracing/telemetry.
Maya Nguyen: looking. GCP health checks for the ILB are flapping in the control plane, healthStatus toggling to UNHEALTHY for endpoints intermittently. GCP console shows API errors for 'compute.healthChecks.get' returning 503/429 in eu-west1 -> paging GCP-status.
GCP Status: We are investigating elevated errors from the Compute API in eu-west1 affecting healthcheck and forwarding rule updates. (ref: https://status.cloud.google.com/incidents/xyz)
Sam Ross: tracing shows KV-cache hits on runtime but the routing layer is failing to resolve local backends intermittently; requests are being routed to fallback pools in us-central, causing TLS negotiation failures and token revalidation errors. Also seeing increased token-introspection failures to our auth provider.
Alex Grady: token introspection failures? That smells like a secondary dependency. @Lucy any idea on auth provider side?
Lucy Chen: I see spikes of 429 on our OAuth introspect endpoint (third-party IDP). It started ~30s after the GCP Compute API errors. Hypothesis: GCP control plane health flapping triggers our reroute logic which causes a storm of session re-validation to IDP.
Emily Carter: cs: getting customer reports—some Private VPC customers in EU are seeing errors and timeouts. I'm drafting a status note to affected accounts. Need an estimated mitigation ETA.
Sam Ross: mitigation plan draft:
- Short term: reduce cross-region failovers by overriding route preference to prefer local backends (temp policy) -> prevents us from hitting fallbacks in us-central.
- Mid term: throttle token-introspection bursts with token cache TTL bump for Private VPC routes.
- Contact GCP to escalate compute API throttling; request healthcheck stability and quota bump.
- Contact IDP to lift introspection rate limits or whitelist our IPs.
Alex Grady: execute short-term first. @Maya please apply routing policy change to pinned routing policy for affected customers (eu-west1). Follow runbook excerpt:
```
# runbook snippets
redwood routing set-policy --project private-vpc --region eu-west1 --policy prefer-local
# revert command
redwood routing set-policy --project private-vpc --region eu-west1 --policy default
```
Maya Nguyen: applying prefer-local to affected projects now. Applying to 6 customer projects sequentially; ETA ~3m. I'll watch health and error rates.
PagerDuty: incident acknowledged by Alex Grady (sev: P1). On-call handoff triggered.
Sam Ross: deploying token-cache TTL bump to 60s for Private VPC traffic to reduce introspection QPS. Pushing change to canary -> rollout.
Lucy Chen: reached out to IDP support, providing logs and spike windows. They responded that they saw a surge and have rate-limits applied, opening ticket #IDP-772. Asking for temporary quota increase.
Maya Nguyen: prefer-local policy applied to first 3 projects. Error rates dropped 70% for those tenants; latency returned to baseline for a subset. Continuing to roll out.
Emily Carter: sending out customer-facing note now. Short note: "We're seeing increased errors for Private VPC customers in EU due to intermittent GCP Compute API errors affecting load balancer health checks. We've applied temporary routing changes to reduce cross-region failovers. We're continuing to monitor and will follow up." Will post to status.redwood.com
Alex Grady: good. @Datadog Bot can you surface an aggregated dashboard link for all affected tenants (errors, latency, token introspect failures)?
Datadog Bot: https://app.datadoghq.com/dashboard/abcdef - aggregated view created. Added alerts for token-introspect 429s and ILB API 5xx.
Sam Ross: can confirm token-introspect 429s dropped after cache bump and routing change. Still seeing occasional 502s from control plane but much less. Proceeding to monitor for 30m.
GCP Status: we've marked the Compute API incident as "under mitigation". Engineers are rolling a fix; ETA ETA 2 hours for full stabilization per upstream.
Alex Grady: action items assigned:
- Maya: finish routing policy rollouts and monitor + revert when stable (done: in progress)
- Sam: monitor caches + telemetry, prepare rollback of ttl when safe (done: canary -> in progress)
- Lucy: follow up with IDP until quota bump confirmed (done: open ticket)
- Emily: CS comms and customer triage list (done: notifying top 10 impacted)
- Alex: coordinate with GCP escalation and decide whether to lift prefer-local after upstream fix (done: in progress)
Sam Ross: adding mitigation note to incident timeline. Pushing a temporary alert suppressor for redundant alerts to avoid alert fatigue.
Emily Carter: listing impacted customers: AcmeCorp (high), Nimbly (medium), FinDelta (high). Outreach in progress.
Maya Nguyen: finished rollouts. All 6 projects on prefer-local. Error rates now at ~5% above baseline vs 40% earlier. No new P1 pages in the last 6m.
Alex Grady: handoff at 17:40 UTC to Maya (networking) for monitoring. I'm stepping off on-call in 20m but will stay on pager until GCP confirms. @PagerDuty please update schedule.
PagerDuty: on-call handover: Alex -> Maya at 17:40 UTC. Notifications updated.
Lucy Chen: IDP replied - temporary introspection quota increased for our IP range. They will keep the ticket open until GCP fully stabilizes traffic patterns.
GCP Status: incident update - mitigation in place, API error rates decreasing. Next update in 30m.
Sam Ross: recommend keeping prefer-local until GCP confirms full recovery; prepare a safe rollback runbook to avoid a sudden surge of token introspection during revert.
Alex Grady: agreed. I'll draft the rollback procedure and post in the runbook repo. Also creating a postmortem placeholder and assigning to Sam + Maya + Lucy + Emily.
Incident Bot: postmortem created: https://docs.internal.redwood/postmortems/incident-1776500000
Emily Carter: sending follow-up note to impacted customers with mitigation details and ETA for final resolution. CS will offer 1:1 calls for high-impact customers.
Maya Nguyen: continuing to monitor; will escalate if error rates rise above 10% again.
Sam Ross: monitoring window continuing. If no regression in 60m we'll move to degraded (P2) and plan a full revert when GCP finishes.
Alex Grady: thanks team. Quick summary so far to put in incident timeline: GCP Compute API errors -> ILB health flaps -> cross-region failovers -> token introspect surge -> IDP rate limits -> apply prefer-local + cache bump -> reduced customer impact. Root cause upstream; follow-up with GCP + IDP.
Lucy Chen: note for postmortem: evaluate whether our reroute logic should include a rate-limiter on token introspections and backoff jitter to avoid cascading third-party rate limits. Also consider backpressure to clients when local backend cannot be confirmed.
Emily Carter: I'll coordinate customer follow-ups and prepare CS notes for postmortem.
Alex Grady: closing this thread for now; will update when GCP signals resolved or if we see regression. Good work. :thumbsup:
